course.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
course.designation: Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science
course.campus: Air University Aerospace & Aviation Campus, Kamra
prerequisites: CS-214L Data Structures and Algorithms Lab

weekly_clo_note: The source course log does not contain a per-session CLO column. Week-level CLO badges in this portal are transparent alignments derived from the approved CLO definitions plus the explicit CLO–assessment mapping; the session topics and assessments themselves are transcribed from the course guide.

weeks.title: Algorithm Foundations
weeks.clo_basis: Derived from the CLO definitions and the session topics; the source course log does not provide a week-level CLO column.

sessions.topic: Course orientation and role of algorithms
sessions.coverage: Course outline, grading, CLOs, why algorithms matter, role of algorithms in computing, examples of algorithmic thinking.
Concept and properties of an algorithm; characteristics; computational problem-solving steps; basic issues related to algorithms.
sessions.activity: Identify algorithm components from everyday/computing examples.

sessions.coverage: Algorithm representation using pseudocode/flowcharts; criterion for analyzing algorithms; proving correctness; pre-condition and post-condition.
sessions.activity: Write a simple algorithm and specify its pre/post-conditions.

weeks.title: Correctness, Loop Invariants & Insertion Sort
weeks.clo_basis: Derived from the CLO definitions and the session topics; the source course log does not provide a week-level CLO column.

sessions.coverage: Correctness of iterative algorithms; initialization, maintenance, termination; constructing and proving a loop invariant.
sessions.activity: Guided proof using a simple loop.

sessions.coverage: Insertion Sort algorithm, dry run, loop invariant for Insertion Sort, correctness argument, initial complexity view.
sessions.activity: Trace Insertion Sort on sample arrays.

sessions.coverage: Recursive thinking; mathematical induction for recursive correctness; base case and inductive step.

weeks.title: Algorithm Analysis Fundamentals
weeks.clo_basis: Supported by Assignment 1 coverage/CLO mapping and by the CLO-1 definition.

sessions.coverage: Nature and size of input; basic operation; running time; time and space complexity; counting operations.
Meaning and use of best-case, worst-case, and average/expected behavior; choosing representative input size.

sessions.topic: Growth of functions and complexity classes
sessions.coverage: Constant, logarithmic, linear, linearithmic, quadratic, polynomial, exponential growth; comparison of growth rates.

weeks.title: Asymptotic Notation & Iterative Analysis
weeks.clo_basis: Supported by Quiz 1 coverage/CLO mapping and by the CLO-1 definition.

sessions.coverage: Asymptotic upper bounds; constants and lower-order terms; formal intuition and practical interpretation.
Lower bounds, tight bounds, non-tight bounds; relationships among asymptotic notations.
Single loops, consecutive loops, nested loops; summation-based analysis; best/worst-case variations.

weeks.title: Recursion & Recurrence Relations
weeks.clo_basis: Supported by the CLO-2 definition and Assignment 2/Quiz 2 coverage mapping.

sessions.coverage: Recursive algorithms; forming a recurrence from algorithm structure; base conditions.
Expansion/iteration and substitution ideas; validating a proposed bound.
Constructing a recurrence tree; per-level cost; number of levels; total cost.

weeks.title: Divide-and-Conquer & Merge Sort
weeks.clo_basis: Supported by Assignment 2 coverage/CLO mapping; the design-strategy aspect also prepares CLO-3.

sessions.coverage: Divide, conquer, combine; generic recurrence; when divide-and-conquer is appropriate; contrast with brute force.
Merge Sort algorithm, merge procedure, recursion structure, dry run, correctness idea.
sessions.activity: Trace and annotate a Merge Sort execution.

sessions.topic: Merge Sort analysis + Master Method overview
sessions.coverage: T(n)=2T(n/2)+Θ(n); recurrence-tree analysis; Master Method form and purpose.
sessions.activity: Connect Merge Sort recurrence to Master Method.

weeks.title: Master Method & Quick Sort
weeks.clo_basis: Supported by Quiz 2 coverage/CLO mapping and by the CLO-2 definition.

sessions.coverage: Cases 1–3, applicability conditions, interpretation of a, b, and f(n), numerical examples.
Quick Sort overview; pivot; partitioning; partition procedure; recursive structure; proof-of-correctness intuition.
sessions.activity: Dry run with different pivot positions.

sessions.coverage: Best, average/expected, and worst cases; randomized Quick Sort; comparison with Merge Sort.

weeks.title: Sorting Families & Pre-Mid Consolidation
weeks.clo_basis: Derived from the Week 8 topics and pre-mid coverage. The Mid-Semester Exam after Week 8 covers CLO-1 to CLO-3 as mapped in the course guide.

sessions.coverage: Algorithms, dry runs, best/worst/average behavior, comparison with Insertion Sort.
Non-comparison sorting; assumptions; procedures; analysis; when linear-time sorting is possible.
sessions.activity: Choose appropriate sorting method for given data.

sessions.coverage: Integrated review: correctness, asymptotic analysis, iterative/recursive analysis, recurrences, divide-and-conquer, Merge/Quick Sort, sorting families.

weeks.title: Heaps & Heap Sort
weeks.clo_basis: Supported by the Quiz 3 coverage/CLO-3 mapping, which includes heaps and AVL topics.

sessions.coverage: Heap as complete binary tree; array representation; min heap, max heap; heap property; applications.
Heapify, build-heap, insertion, extract-min/max, deletion; operation costs.
Heap Sort procedure; complexity; in-place behavior; comparison with other sorting algorithms; priority-queue applications.

weeks.title: AVL Trees & Algorithm-Design Strategies
weeks.clo_basis: Supported by the CLO-3 definition and Assignment 3/Quiz 3 coverage mapping.

sessions.coverage: Height-balanced search trees; balance factor; single rotations; double rotations; insertion examples.
sessions.activity: Perform LL, RR, LR, RL rotations.

sessions.coverage: Brute force, divide-and-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming; identifying optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems.
Greedy-choice property; constructing greedy solutions; examples; strengths and limitations; comparison with dynamic programming.

weeks.title: Dynamic Programming
weeks.clo_basis: Supported by the CLO-3 definition and Quiz 3/Assignment 3 coverage mapping.

sessions.coverage: Optimal substructure; overlapping subproblems; recurrence formulation; memoization vs tabulation; DP workflow.
sessions.activity: Convert recursive relation to a DP table.

sessions.coverage: State definition, recurrence, base cases, table construction, solution reconstruction, complexity.
Matrix-chain cost minimization; Longest Common Subsequence recurrence and table; applications.

weeks.title: Graph Representation, BFS & DFS
weeks.clo_basis: The graph topics align with CLO-4; Assignment 3 explicitly includes early graph work under CLO-3 in the assessment calendar.

sessions.coverage: Graph terminology; directed/undirected and weighted graphs; adjacency matrix/list; search goals and connectivity.
sessions.activity: Represent the same graph in multiple forms.

sessions.coverage: Queue-based BFS; BFS tree; distances; shortest path in unweighted graphs; undirected connectivity.
Recursive/stack DFS; discovery structure; connected components; comparison with BFS.

weeks.title: Minimum Spanning Trees & Huffman Coding
weeks.clo_basis: MST topics align with CLO-4; Huffman coding is a greedy-design application aligned with CLO-3. Assignment 4 is mapped to CLO-4.

sessions.coverage: MST concept; growing an MST; cut intuition; Prim’s algorithm; priority-queue perspective; complexity.
Kruskal’s algorithm; sorted edges; cycle avoidance / disjoint sets concept; complexity; Prim vs Kruskal.
Lossless compression idea; prefix codes; Huffman tree construction; code assignment; compression/decompression workflow.
sessions.activity: Build Huffman codes for sample frequencies.

weeks.title: Shortest-Path Algorithms
weeks.clo_basis: Supported directly by the CLO-4 definition and Quiz 4/Assignment 4 coverage mapping.

sessions.coverage: Shortest-path problem; relaxation idea; Dijkstra’s algorithm; assumptions; correctness intuition; complexity.
Negative edges; repeated relaxation; negative-cycle detection; shortest paths in directed acyclic graphs.
Dynamic-programming formulation; distance matrix updates; complexity; comparison of shortest-path algorithms.

weeks.title: String Matching, TSP & Complexity Classes
weeks.clo_basis: CLO-1 includes hard problems; CLO-4 includes heuristic approaches. The final exam is mapped to CLO-3–4 in the assessment calendar.

sessions.coverage: Naive context; Rabin–Karp hashing; spurious hits; string matching with finite automata; examples and comparison.
TSP formulation; brute-force view; heuristic approaches; motivation for hard problems; polynomial-time reductions and completeness idea.
sessions.activity: Discuss exact vs heuristic solution trade-offs.

sessions.coverage: Polynomial-time solvable problems; P, NP, NP-Hard, NP-Complete; differentiation; relationship to reductions; comprehensive final review.
